name: LM393 reed switch sensor module (DO)
description: Magnet detector: a normally-open glass reed switch read by an LM393 comparator, with a sensitivity trimmer, a power LED and a DO LED. DO is HIGH with no magnet and goes LOW (DO LED lit) while a magnet within about 1.5 cm closes the reed (active low). The LM393's open-collector output is pulled up to VCC by 10 kOhm on the board. On/off only, no field strength. Runs on 3.3-5 V. Sold as: SunFounder / generic blue LM393 reed switch sensor module (32 x 14 mm, normally-open glass reed, 10 kOhm trimmer, PWR-LED and DO-LED; 3-pin header VCC, GND, DO).
eli5: A tiny glass switch closes when a magnet comes near, and a little chip turns that into a clean on/off signal so your board knows a door or lid is shut.

buildNotes: Header order as printed: VCC, GND, DO (VCC next to the PWR-LED).
On an ESP32 or Pico power VCC from 3V3: the 10 kOhm pull-up takes DO to VCC, so a 5 V supply puts 5 V on the GPIO.
DO is active LOW: 1 with no magnet, 0 (DO-LED lit) while a magnet closes the reed.
If DO never changes, set the trimmer to mid-range; the reed pulls the comparator input fully to 0 V or VCC.
Hold the magnet alongside the glass tube within about 1.5 cm; don't bend the reed leads close to the glass.
Different from the passive KY-021 (S, +, - order, no comparator).

driver.code:
# LM393 reed switch sensor module (3-pin VCC / GND / DO), MicroPython driver.
# Board circuit (SunFounder schematic): a normally-open reed switch pulls the LM393's
# + input to GND (10 kOhm pull-up to VCC, 100 nF across the reed); the blue 10 kOhm
# trimmer sets the - input. The LM393 open-collector output has a 10 kOhm pull-up to
# VCC and drives the DO-LED (1 kOhm), so:
#   DO HIGH (1) with no magnet (reed open, DO-LED off)
#   DO LOW  (0) while a magnet closes the reed (DO-LED lit)  -> "magnet"
# The reeds bounce for a few ms at each change; the 100 nF cap smooths most of it,
# and magnet() also waits for a stable level. Power VCC from 3.3 V on a 3.3 V board,
# because DO is pulled up to VCC.
from machine import Pin
import time


class ReedModule:
    def __init__(self, pin, debounce_ms=20):
        """pin: GPIO number (or Pin) wired to DO."""
        # The board has its own 10 kOhm pull-up on DO, so no internal pull is needed.
        self.pin = Pin(pin, Pin.IN) if isinstance(pin, int) else pin
        self.debounce_ms = debounce_ms

    def raw(self):
        """Logic level on DO right now: 0 = magnet (reed closed), 1 = no magnet."""
        return self.pin.value()

    def closed(self):
        """True while DO is LOW (reed closed by a magnet), undebounced."""
        return self.pin.value() == 0

    def magnet(self):
        """Debounced: True if DO stays LOW for debounce_ms."""
        state = self.pin.value()
        t0 = time.ticks_ms()
        while time.ticks_diff(time.ticks_ms(), t0) < self.debounce_ms:
            v = self.pin.value()
            if v != state:
                state = v
                t0 = time.ticks_ms()
            time.sleep_ms(2)
        return state == 0

    def irq(self, handler, on_close=True):
        """Call handler(pin) when a magnet arrives (falling edge) or, with
        on_close=False, when it leaves (rising edge). Bounce can give extra calls."""
        self.pin.irq(handler=handler, trigger=Pin.IRQ_FALLING if on_close else Pin.IRQ_RISING)

# LM393 reed switch sensor module (VCC / GND / DO)

## Overview
The blue **reed switch sensor module** (SunFounder / generic "reed sensor module", 32 x 14 mm) carries a glass **normally-open reed switch** on long leads, an **LM393 comparator**, a blue 10 kΩ **trimmer**, a PWR-LED and a DO-LED. Unlike the bare KY-021, the comparator gives a clean, buffered output.
- **DO is HIGH with no magnet and goes LOW (DO-LED lit) while a magnet closes the reed** (active low)
- Magnet within about 1.5 cm of the glass tube
- On/off only: no field strength

## Pinout (3-pin header, as printed)
| Pin | Name | Function |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | VCC | Supply 3.3-5 V |
| 2 | GND | Ground |
| 3 | DO | Digital output: 1 = no magnet, 0 = magnet (10 kΩ pull-up to VCC) |

## Electrical limits
- Supply **3.3-5 V** (vendor rating; the LM393 itself runs on 2-36 V). About 3-6 mA with the LEDs.
- DO is the LM393 open-collector output pulled up to VCC by 10 kΩ: **power from 3.3 V on an ESP32 or Pico** so DO never exceeds 3.3 V.

## Interface details
Circuit (SunFounder schematic): reed switch from the LM393 + input to GND, 10 kΩ pull-up to VCC and 100 nF across the reed; trimmer wiper on the - input.
```
reed open   -> + input = VCC > trimmer -> output off -> DO = 1
reed closed -> + input = 0 V < trimmer -> output low -> DO = 0, DO-LED on
```
The trimmer only needs to sit somewhere between the ends; the reed itself decides. If DO never changes, turn the trimmer to mid-range.

## Wiring
| Module | ESP32 | Raspberry Pi Pico | Raspberry Pi 4 |
|---|---|---|---|
| VCC | 3V3 | 3V3(OUT) (pin 36) | 3V3 (pin 1) |
| GND | GND | GND | GND (pin 6) |
| DO | GPIO27 | GP15 | GPIO24 (pin 18) |

## Using the driver
```python
from reed_module import ReedModule
import time
reed = ReedModule(27)           # GPIO wired to DO
while True:
    print('Magnet: %s' % ('YES' if reed.magnet() else 'no'))
    time.sleep(0.5)
```
`magnet()` is debounced (20 ms stable); `raw()` / `closed()` read instantly; `irq(handler)` fires on the falling edge when a magnet arrives.

## Gotchas
- **VCC is pin 1 and DO pin 3**: reversing the header puts the supply on DO.
- Don't power VCC from 5 V with a 3.3 V board (DO is pulled up to VCC).
- The glass reed is fragile; don't bend its leads close to the glass. Hold the magnet alongside the tube.
- Not to be confused with the passive KY-021 (S, +, - order, no comparator).

## Datasheet
LM393: https://www.ti.com/lit/ds/symlink/lm393.pdf
Module schematic, photo and behaviour: https://docs.sunfounder.com/projects/raphael-kit/en/latest/_shared/component/cpn_reed_switch_module.html
